paras: The attempted lynching of Daniel Wolfe was an attack by a crowd on a prisoner at Urbana, Illinois, in late October 1881, in which Wolfe was dragged from an officers' wagon with a rope around his neck. Officers cut the rope and lodged him in jail, and the only account of the episode, carried by the Dallas Herald, does not give his race.

According to the Dallas daily herald, Wolfe had just been released from the Illinois penitentiary after serving a sixteen years' sentence. He was accused of persuading a young woman "of good character" to go with him by telling her she would stay with his family while he visited Indiana. The paper said he had no home to take her to and instead forced her to stay all night with him in a haystack in the country.

The young woman escaped the next morning and told her story at home, and a crowd at once set out after Wolfe and caught him after a long chase. He was taken before a magistrate, who committed him to jail.

On the way to the jail, what the paper called "an incensed crowd" attacked him, threw a rope over his neck and dragged him from the wagon and across the road to hang him. He was badly bruised, but the officers cut the rope, rescued him and lodged him in jail "despite the efforts of the would-be lynchers." The account gives no exact date beyond "a few days ago" and no size for the crowd.
No report of arrests in the crowd, or of a trial of Wolfe on the accusation, appears in the coverage.

The Dallas daily herald ran the story on 30 October 1881 as an unattributed paragraph, and the Dallas weekly herald reprinted it word for word on 3 November. The item treated the accusation as established, called Wolfe "the wretch" and described the woman's account as a "story of sorrow and distress." It reported the officers' rescue without comment on the crowd, and it mentioned no one's race.
No account from an Illinois paper and no Black-press report appear in the coverage.

reader.title: Attempted lynching of Daniel Wolfe
bases: A crowd threw a rope over Wolfe's neck and dragged him from the wagon to hang him before officers cut the rope (A1); an attempted lynching.

An 'incensed crowd' tried to hang Wolfe over an accusation involving a young woman, but officers cut the rope and he survived (A1); no one was killed, so this was an attempt, not a lynching under the standard definition.
Only one original text was found, the Dallas daily herald item (A1); the Dallas weekly herald's is the same text reprinted (A2).

accounts.label: Unattributed news item (Dallas Herald)
accounts.gist: Wolfe lured a young woman away and kept her overnight in a haystack; a crowd chased and caught him, and on the way to jail another crowd tried to hang him until officers cut the rope.

framing.detail: Treats the accusation as fact and calls Wolfe 'the wretch' and the crowd 'incensed', but describes the officers rescuing him 'despite the efforts of the would-be lynchers' without comment on the attempt.

record_check.dossier: The article names only Urbana, Illinois, not a county; Champaign is inferred from the town name, not stated
Not stated; the article names no race for Wolfe, the woman or the crowd

Pursuit and capture, then a rope thrown over his neck and dragging toward a hanging that officers stopped; 'beating' is a stretch (he was bruised by the dragging), and 'hanging' was attempted, not carried out
Supported: he was attacked while officers were taking him to jail after a magistrate committed him

record_check.record: accused of forcing a young woman to stay overnight with him in a haystack
record_check.dossier: Supported; the article also says he lured her away by 'plausible tales' that he would take her to his family
